mechanism_narrative: The recent two-week upward trend in RETAIL_REC, from -41.9 to -34.1, indicates a gradual return of discretionary activity that will continue to improve over the next four weeks, driving the mean higher.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days averages below -34.1, indicating a reversal of the recent upward trend.

mechanism_narrative: As WORKPLACES mobility approaches -25% from baseline, it signals a critical mass of people returning to offices, which will drive increased demand for nearby retail and recreation over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: WORKPLACES rises above -28% but RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days decreases compared to the last 28 days.

mechanism_narrative: A simultaneous increase in TRANSIT and PARKS mobility suggests people are venturing out more for both leisure and commuting, creating a synergistic effect that boosts retail and recreation activity over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: TRANSIT and PARKS both increase week-on-week by more than 2 points
failure_condition: Both TRANSIT and PARKS increase by more than 2 points week-on-week, but RETAIL_REC over the next 14 days falls.

mechanism_narrative: In a regime of easing restrictions, the sustained high level of RESIDENTIAL mobility, combined with its recent slight decline, indicates a shift towards more outdoor activities, which will divert some spending from home-based consumption to retail and recreation over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RESIDENTIAL mobility remains high or increases, but RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days does not improve compared to the last 28 days.

mechanism_narrative: Despite minor fluctuations, the overall low levels of WORKPLACES and TRANSIT mobility, remaining significantly below baseline, indicate a persistent reluctance to return to pre-pandemic routines, which will continue to suppress retail and recreation activity over the next four weeks.
failure_condition: RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days significantly improves, despite WORKPLACES and TRANSIT remaining below -25% and -30% respectively.

mechanism_narrative: The recent sharp decline in PARKS mobility followed by a rebound (from -38.4 to -31.3) suggests a short-term increase in outdoor leisure, which will temporarily boost related retail and recreation over the next week before stabilizing.
candidate_trigger: PARKS increases by more than 5 points week-on-week
failure_condition: PARKS increases by more than 5 points week-on-week, but RETAIL_REC over the next 7 days declines.

mechanism_narrative: The persistent positive GROCERY_PHARM mobility combined with significantly negative RETAIL_REC indicates a continued prioritization of essential trips over discretionary spending, suggesting RETAIL_REC will remain suppressed over the next four weeks.
candidate_trigger: GROCERY_PHARM remains positive while RETAIL_REC remains below -30%
failure_condition: GROCERY_PHARM remains positive and RETAIL_REC remains below -30%, but RETAIL_REC over the next 28 days significantly improves.

mechanism_narrative: A sustained decline in RESIDENTIAL mobility over two consecutive weeks, indicating fewer people staying home, will eventually translate into increased outdoor activity and a boost for retail and recreation over the next two weeks.
candidate_trigger: RESIDENTIAL falls by more than 1 point for two consecutive weeks
failure_condition: RESIDENTIAL mobility declines for two consecutive weeks, but RETAIL_REC over the next 14 days does not improve compared to the last 14 days.
